chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Muslim said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And the chaste women from the women except what your right hands possess.' He said: 'It is that a man commands his slave and his concubine is under him, so he says to him: 'Separate from your wife and do not approach her.' Then he keeps her away from him until she menstruates, then he touches her. If she menstruates after he touches her, he returns her to him without a new marriage contract.'

key_terms.مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُكُمْ: What your right hands possess (concubines/slave women)

ai.seo_question: How does the master's command affect the marital status of a slave woman according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the specific mechanics of *tamlik* (ownership) and marital rights within the master-slave dynamic, interpreting the exception in Surah An-Nisa regarding 'what your right hands possess.' It details a procedural sequence where a master can temporarily separate a slave-wife from her slave-husband, use physical intimacy to establish a state of purity, and subsequently return her to the marriage without a new *nikah*, highlighting the flexibility of marital bonds under ownership. This ruling underscores the distinct legal status of slave-wives compared to free women, a key topic in Shia fiqh regarding the dissolution and re-establishment of marriage through ownership rights.
